about: Juno's annotations, an invented case. Every participant turn in order, found by its opening words: its experiential statements and each one's key quote, quote and statement in the same order, a gap in a quote marked with an ellipsis, its exploratory note and the words highlighted, or no statement for a turn with a note alone. Then the times of the work and her PET board. make_demo.py builds the workbook from Juno's interview CSV, then her progress file and her themes file from this.

turns.at: Erm. That is a big question
es: A house never empty with the dog, even when quiet
turns.en: Twice: just there. The stair is a boundary kept without being asked for. Quiet and empty come apart here, so presence is felt rather than seen.
kq: I suppose she is just there. That is the first thing. Bramble is just there, all the time. … The house is never empty now. Even when it is quiet it is not empty.
turns.crux: Even when it is quiet it is not empty

turns.at: It is like being caught
es: Caught out going soft over the dog
turns.en: Caught, as if found out. Four years of no dog, then a whole conversation in a dressing gown. She laughs at the state of herself and keeps groaning back.
kq: It is like being caught. I am not a soppy person, or I did not think I was. … And I have started groaning back at her. That is the state of me now.

turns.at: My partner wore me down
es: Won over by the dog before she would admit it
turns.en: The photograph wins before the argument is over. Two stories of who decided, and she keeps both. The lean in the yard is the lean at the door now.
kq: once you have seen a photograph like that you have already lost the argument, you just have not admitted it yet. … I still say I was talked into her, and my partner still says I was the one who filled the form in, and we are both right.

turns.at: Right. So the alarm goes
turns.en: Who gets up is the house's first question, and not always friendly. The whine outlasts them both. Cracking is her word, said against herself.

turns.at: Annoying. No, it is more than annoying
es: Always the one up for the dog, and feeling taken for granted
turns.en: She corrects her own word upwards. Twelve minutes stand for for ever. The wag takes the annoyance away, and losing it is its own annoyance.
kq: Annoying. No, it is more than annoying. … It is what the twelve minutes says. That I will always go. That they know I will always go, and so they can lie there and let me.

turns.at: I would. Because then I could have it out
es: Anger taken off her by the dog, so it never gets said
turns.en: A mood cannot be carried down those stairs. What goes unsaid between the two of them is counted in years.
kq: But you cannot carry a mood down those stairs. She takes it off you at the bottom. … So it never gets said. Five years of it never getting said.
turns.crux: She takes it off you at the bottom

turns.at: It is the same walk.
turns.en: The route given in full, as if walked again in the telling. Five years of the empty gap, and still she has to check.

turns.at: I love it. I did not expect
es: From resenting the morning walk to loving it as her own time
Glad to be out of reach with the dog
turns.en: Resentment turned to love over the years, and it surprises her to say so. Out with the dog nobody can ask her for anything. Her head goes quiet by watching, not by thinking.
kq: I love it. I did not expect to hear myself say that. The first year I resented it, I really did, I thought, this is forty minutes I have not got. And now it is the bit of the day that is mine.
Nobody can ask me for anything, because I am out with the dog, and that is a completely respectable reason to be unavailable. Nobody argues with it.
turns.crux: it is the bit of the day that is mine

turns.at: Yes. It sounds ridiculous
es: The dog's joy quieting her head and her moods
The dog like a child who will never grow away from her
turns.en: Ten past seven, in February, every morning. The joy is the dog's and it reaches her. The child she compares her to never grows up and away.
kq: But there is something about how much she is enjoying it. … And you cannot stand next to that much enthusiasm for a hedge and stay in a bad mood, it is not possible.
It is a bit like being with a small child, except she is not going to grow out of it and start being embarrassed by me.

turns.at: On the bottom field, yes.
es: The dog's joy worth the worry
turns.en: One of the best things she has seen, and furious the whole time: two at once again. She weighs it up every morning and always lets go.
kq: I have watched her go across that field after a hare and it is one of the best things I have ever seen, and I am furious the entire time it is happening. … because the look on her at full stretch is worth more to me than the twenty minutes of worry.

turns.at: Erm. Yes. The first year was hard.
es: Regretting the dog in a hard first year, her time no longer hers
turns.en: Not the money but the freedom. A weekend away becomes a logistics operation. The mistake is thought, and kept silent.
kq: The first year was hard. I had not reckoned on how much of my time stopped being mine. … And there was a stretch, maybe six months in, where I thought, I have made a mistake here. I did not say that out loud to anybody.

turns.at: Because it is a terrible thing to say
es: Unable to say she regrets a dog with a hard past
The regret gone, mostly, but back on wet winter nights
turns.en: Saying it would be terrible because of what the dog has been through. It went away, mostly. On a wet Sunday at ten it comes back.
kq: Because it is a terrible thing to say, isn't it. She is a rescue. She had a rough time of it before us, you can still see it in her, she flinches if you move your arm too fast above her head, even now.
So I did not say it, and then it went away, mostly, the way things do. But I would be lying if I told you it never comes back. It comes back on a Sunday night in February when it is chucking it down

turns.at: There was one. It was proper rain
es: Moved by the dog waiting on her decision
turns.en: Stillness on both sides of the porch. That the dog waited without pushing is what got her. The turn at the postbox is made by neither of them.
kq: And she was sat behind me, completely still, not pushing at me, not doing the whine, just waiting to see what I decided. That is the bit that got me, actually. She was not begging. She was just waiting.
turns.crux: She was not begging. She was just waiting.

turns.at: I think because it cost me something.
es: Closest to the dog on the night it cost her
turns.en: She hears herself sound grand and says it anyway. Cost as proof. Failing together turns into a bargain struck by the postbox.
kq: I think because it cost me something. That sounds a bit grand. But the easy days do not prove anything, do they.

turns.at: Well, she has not signed anything.
es: Unspoken rules with the dog, strange to have
turns.en: The joke first, then the list of the rules. An understanding with no conversation, which strikes her as strange once she stops to think.
kq: There are rules in that house and neither of us wrote them down. That is a strange thing to have with another creature, when you stop and think about it. We have never once had a conversation and we both know exactly where we stand.

turns.at: Oh, it is the best bit of the day
es: The dog's welcome home the best bit of her day
turns.en: Coming home given in sound first, then in weight. The same lean as the yard five years ago. The rabbit muffles the whine.
kq: Oh, it is the best bit of the day, without question. … She puts her whole weight against your legs and stands there with her head down.

turns.at: It is being wanted. Plainly.
es: Wanted as by nobody else
turns.en: Plainly, and with no bitterness, she insists. The hello from the other room is set beside it: fine, what adults do.
kq: It is being wanted. Plainly. Nobody else in my life is that pleased to see me, and I say that with no bitterness at all, it is just a fact.

turns.at: I think it makes me come home.
es: From finding reasons to stay out to coming home for the dog
turns.en: A stretch of staying out, said lightly, nothing dramatic. Now she wants the door bit. Her partner has noticed.
kq: There was a stretch where I would find reasons to stay out, nothing dramatic, just one more thing to sort out before I left. And now there is a clock on me. … But I want the door bit. So I come home.

turns.at: They said it once, in passing.
es: Unsettled by her partner's remark that she comes home for the dog
turns.en: Said nicely and heard twice over. She does not know what to do with it, and will not deny it.
kq: And they were pleased, I think, they meant it nicely. But there was something else in it as well, which was, you will come home for the dog. And I did not know what to do with that. Because it is true.

turns.at: Uncomfortable. But not in a way I could argue with
es: Finding the dog easier than people, and not liking what that says
turns.en: The thought she keeps landing on and moving off. The dog needs nothing to have been got right. With a person the past is stood in the hall as well.
kq: The dog is easier. That is the thing I keep landing on and then moving off, because it is not a nice thing to think about yourself. She does not need me to have got anything right.

turns.at: Yes. Because I do not know what to do with it.
es: Unsure whether the dog is good for the couple or a way of not talking
turns.en: Two readings held open, good for us or a way round each other. Some weeks the one, some weeks the other.
kq: Either it means she has been very good for us … Or it means we have found something to talk about instead of talking. And I genuinely do not know which one it is.

turns.at: Yes. So in the spring she came up lame
turns.en: A lurcher is all leg, so a back leg is not nothing. The sums she does on the way are about the end.

turns.at: My hands were shaking on the wheel
es: Shaken by fear for the dog, and by how much she has come to matter
turns.en: Her competence gone, her voice a stranger's. The dog's silence read as knowing. Underneath, the question of when this happened.
kq: My hands were shaking on the wheel, which surprised me. I am usually all right in an emergency, I am the one people ring. … And underneath all of it there was this other thing going on, which was, when did I let something matter this much.

turns.at: Well. It was a thorn.
es: Tears of relief held back until the car park
turns.en: Bathos, told against herself. The tears kept for the car. Not embarrassment, shock, she corrects.
kq: And I sat in the car afterwards and cried, which I had not done in the waiting room, I saved that up for the car park. Relief, obviously.

turns.at: It was out of proportion.
es: Grief for the dog found ready in advance, and not welcome
turns.en: Grief already prepared. She is six, and lurchers are not a forty year proposition. The rehearsal tells her it is coming.
kq: She had a thorn in her foot and I had spent twenty minutes organising my own grief in advance, in traffic. … So that Saturday was a rehearsal. And I did not enjoy finding out that I have got the whole thing ready to go.
turns.crux: So that Saturday was a rehearsal.

turns.at: I try not to.
es: Trying not to think of the dog's death, and laughing herself out of it
turns.en: Not much of an answer, she says. The running legs, and the thought she stops. She laughs herself out of it.
kq: I try not to. I am aware that is not much of an answer. It sits there. … it is a waste of a Tuesday evening to sit there grieving a dog who is snoring at you.

turns.at: Oh, the groomer. Yes.
turns.en: Lighter, by request. The dog's disgust told with relish. Two hours set up as a gift.

turns.at: Nothing. That is the honest answer.
es: Lost in a wrong quiet without the dog
turns.en: The free time does not arrive. The quiet is wrong, a noise only noticed once it stops. The stair again, empty now.
kq: The first time I thought, brilliant, two hours, I will get so much done. And I came back into the house and stood in the kitchen and did not know what to do with myself. It was so quiet. And it was not a nice quiet, it was a wrong quiet

turns.at: Er. It was like the house was on standby.
es: The house 'on standby' without the dog
turns.en: Standby, then a set: the house not lived in without her. Nothing was decided, it was arranged. The rule on the chair is going the way of the others.
kq: Er. It was like the house was on standby. Everything in it is arranged around her now, and we never sat down and decided to arrange it. … And with her not in it the whole place was just a set. Furniture waiting for somebody.
turns.crux: It was like the house was on standby.

turns.at: Yes. And I did not like it at all.
turns.en: She cannot wait the two hours out. Alarming, she says, only once it is said aloud to somebody.

turns.at: I suppose because of how much is resting on her.
es: A bit alarming, how much of home rests on the dog
turns.en: Two hours flat, and then what of longer. All of it on someone who cannot know she carries it.
kq: I suppose because of how much is resting on her. If a house can go flat for two hours, what happens when it is not two hours. That is the thought I do not let myself finish.

turns.at: We do. Constantly.
es: Real fun in doing the dog's voices together
turns.en: Laughter she defends as real, and then times. Half nine: when the voices come out.
kq: It is genuinely the funniest thing in that house. And I do think that is real, that is not us avoiding anything, that is just a good thing we have got hold of.

turns.at: Money. The fact that neither of us
es: Escaping hard talk through the dog
turns.en: The list given in full, for once: money, next year, her mother. The chin on the knee as the legitimate way out.
kq: There is a list. … But the dog is a very good door to close on it. She comes and puts her chin on your knee at about that time, and it is completely legitimate to stop talking and make a fuss of her instead.

turns.at: Two ways at once
es: Relieved by the dog's interruption, then a bit uneasy at the relief
The dog the reason the couple share a room at all
turns.en: She names her own pattern, two ways at once. Separate floors before her, and now the sofa with a dog laid between them.
kq: Relieved, because I do not want to do the list at half nine either. And then a bit uneasy, because being relieved is a sign of something, isn't it.
But then I think, she is also the reason we are in the same room at all. Before her we would be on separate floors doing separate things and calling it an evening.

turns.at: Good, because I cannot.
turns.en: Glad not to be asked to settle it. The answer moves with the week she has had.

turns.at: In the kitchen. That was the rule
es: Goodnight to the dog out loud: a ridiculous ritual she could not skip
turns.en: The rule held, more or less. The blanket was hers once. Two thumps counted exactly, and a ritual she could not skip.
kq: And the last thing that happens every night is that I go in and say goodnight to her, out loud, like she is a person … It is the most ridiculous ritual and if I ever skipped it I think I would lie there upstairs thinking about it.

turns.at: Erm. Probably the regret
es: More patience for the dog than for the people at home, and she knows it
turns.en: Two things unsaid, the first year and her unevenness. She knows it and does not know what to do about it.
kq: And maybe the other one, which is that I know I am kinder to her than I am to the people in my house. … I do not know what to do about that, but I do know it.
turns.crux: I know I am kinder to her than I am to the people in my house

turns.at: Fine, actually.
turns.en: She makes it ordinary: what most people with a dog would say with nobody they live with listening.

turns.at: Erm. Only that it is very ordinary.
es: The dog become part of home through ordinary days
turns.en: Her own summary, ordinary and wet. There was no day it happened. Home is described with the dog in it, without a thought first.
kq: None of this is dramatic. … And somewhere in all that ordinary stuff she has got herself right into the middle of the house, and I could not tell you which day that happened. There was no day. It is just that now, if you asked me to describe home, she would be in the description
